current_date: Effective for all planning applications received from 1 April 2020
current_evidence: Grokbot's old 'planning-and-building-control/building-or-improving-your-property' URL now resolves to the 'planning-building-and-environment/applications-permission-and-advice' path. The parent 'How to prepare a valid planning application' guide presents this web page as the Local Validation List, says it applies from 1 April 2020, and links no newer list or PDF.

issues.detail: The workbook URL uses Buckinghamshire's old site path and redirects to the new path. It works today, but the workbook should store the new URL. Several docs_read and source links already mix the old and new paths.

Grokbot records List date as null and 'Undated'. The parent guide page dates the list as effective from 1 April 2020, which makes it more than 6 years old, so 'Outdated (>2y)?' should read yes, although the list is still the one in force.
issues.evidence: Parent page: the Local Validation List 'will come into effect for all planning applications received from 1 April 2020'.

issues.detail: Grokbot treats items from the 'Additional supporting documents' page as validation requirements. That page says none of them is required for validation. Affected rows: Crime prevention strategy, Daylight/Sunlight, Energy/Sustainability statement, Noise impact assessment, Open space assessment, Parking plan, Statement of Community Involvement, Street scene drawings, Floor plans/internal elevations and Schedule of works (all under Full planning); Drainage strategy and Foul sewage statement (under Householder); Lighting assessment (under Listed building consent).
issues.evidence: Additional supporting documents page: 'these documents are not required for validation' but 'you are encouraged to submit them with your initial application where they are relevant'.

issues.detail: All 12 tab_items are guidance links, policy-reference tables or text fragments, not requirements. They are also mislabelled 'Submission rules' or 'Local forms / checklists'. Examples: 'Historic England's guidance on Statements of Heritage Significance... Find out if your application contains a heritage asset:'; 'NPPF paragraph 83 Local Plan Area Policy reference Aylesbury Vale No policy Chiltern GB2...'; 'Hydrology in Burnham Beeches (PDF, 715 KB).'; 'For local guidance, see the guidance note on Planning Applications for Wind Energy Developments'; a list of tree guidance PDFs.
issues.evidence: The Supporting information page gives a 'Do' checklist, a policy table and a 'Guidance and next steps' block under each requirement. Grokbot captured these blocks instead of the requirement headings and triggers.

issues.detail: The two Householder rows (Drainage Strategy/SuDS and Foul Sewage/Utilities Statement) come from a sentence that expressly excludes householder extensions. Grokbot's note 'Application type named in requirement text' matched the word 'householder' inside the exclusion. The foul drainage assessment is also advisory only.
issues.evidence: 'You should submit a Foul Drainage Assessment for any development (other than householder extensions) where the development involves the disposal of foul sewage...'

issues.detail: The only Listed building consent row is Lighting Assessment, matched because 'listed buildings' appears in the text, and that assessment is advisory. The real LBC requirements are not placed there. The Design and access statement is required for all LBC applications, and the Heritage statement is required wherever heritage assets are present.
issues.evidence: Supporting information: Design and access statement 'required for... all listed building consent applications'; Heritage statement 'required for applications that contain designated or non-designated heritage assets'.

issues.detail: About 27 requirements were put under Full planning by inference ('INFERRED... placed under Full planning'), and Outline, Advertisement consent and the other types were marked '(none)'. The source says the Local Validation List covers householder, full, outline, minerals and waste, listed building consent and advertisement consent applications, and its triggers depend on location and scale, not type. For example, the Heritage statement and FRA apply equally to householder schemes with heritage assets or in Flood Zone 2/3. The Ecology & Trees checklist applies to all types. Affordable housing, Planning statement and Transport assessment apply to outline schemes too.
issues.evidence: Parent page: 'The Local Validation List for Buckinghamshire Council applies to the following application types: householder, full, outline planning permission, minerals and waste development, listed building consent, advertisement consent'.

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts quote the 'Why you need...' rationale instead of the actual trigger, so the thresholds are lost. Correct triggers: Affordable housing applies at AV 11+ dwellings or 0.3ha+; Chiltern/South Bucks 5+ homes in the AONB, 10+ homes or 0.5ha+; Wycombe 10+ dwellings or more than 1,000 sq m. Air quality applies to all proposals in an AQMA (excluding householders), majors in settlements with an AQMA, majors requiring EIA, and all minerals and waste. The Heritage statement applies where designated or non-designated heritage assets are present. The Planning statement applies to all major applications. The Sequential test applies in Flood Zones 2/3 to new dwellings or non-residential schemes over 250 sq m. Ecology report applies when the Ecology & Trees checklist says one is needed. Transport statement/assessment applies at C3 50-80 / 80+ dwellings under Highways DM thresholds. Travel plan applies at C3 80+ units.
issues.evidence: e.g. Grokbot Affordable Housing trigger: 'This is a local requirement and is needed to assess whether affordable housing policies will be met' vs source 'required for applications meeting affordable housing thresholds'.

issues.detail: The 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' row under Minerals & waste takes its trigger from the Air quality assessment bullets ('major applications that require an EIA', 'all minerals and waste applications'). The source does not say every minerals or waste application needs an EIA. The EIA trigger is Schedule 1 of the 2017 EIA Regulations, plus Schedule 2 proposals likely to have significant effects.
issues.evidence: Grokbot excerpt: 'require an EIA all minerals and waste applications'; source EIA: 'It is required for all proposals defined under Schedule 1 of the 2017 regulations'.

issues.detail: Several excerpts are cut off or come from a different requirement. Agricultural dwelling appraisal and ALC/Soils both read 'and proposed Agricultural Land Classification is required.' The real Agricultural statement trigger is 'all agricultural applications, and proposals involving an agricultural holding'. Employment/Economic Statement reads only 'of necessary employment land.' LVIA opens with 'PR16) Note:'. 'Existing and proposed site levels / sections' and 'Landscaping scheme' are both minerals restoration and aftercare text. 'Ground investigation / Geotechnical / Basement Impact Assessment' is the minerals hydrological assessment for dewatering, which has nothing to do with basements. 'Statement of Community Involvement' is cut off at 'all large ma'.
issues.evidence: Source: hydrological and hydrogeological assessment 'needed for applications for minerals and waste development where dewatering is proposed'.

issues.detail: The Mineral assessment trigger is filed under 'Minerals & waste (county)', but it applies to non-mineral development (housing and similar) inside a Mineral Safeguarding Area, so it belongs under Full/Outline planning.
issues.evidence: 'Proposals in a Mineral Safeguarding Area are needed for: 10 or more dwellings or 0.5ha or more in size (within in an urban area) 2 or more dwellings (outside of an urban area)' - 'to prevent the unnecessary sterilisation of minerals as a result of non-mineral development'.

issues.detail: These validation requirements on the Supporting information page were not captured. Flood risk assessment: Flood Zone 2 or 3, or over 1ha in Flood Zone 1. SuDS statement: all majors, minors of 3+ dwellings, or sites at medium/high surface water flood risk or containing an ordinary watercourse. Community needs assessment: loss of a community facility. Equestrian statement: all equestrian applications. New dwellings schedule: any new dwellings. Structural/building condition survey: substantial demolition or renovation, e.g. barn conversions in Green Belt or AONB. Tree canopy calculator: 0.5ha+ outside a designated town centre, Wycombe area only. Trees report: per the Ecology & Trees checklist. Waste and recycling strategy: all minor and major applications. Water environment assessment: Source Protection Zones and Drinking Water Safeguard Zones. Town centre impact assessment: retail/leisure over AV 2,000 sq m; Chiltern/South Bucks 1,000 sq m; Wycombe 1,000/500/250 sq m or all, depending on location.
issues.evidence: Supporting information page headings: 'Community needs assessment', 'Equestrian statement', 'New dwellings schedule', 'Structural or building condition survey', 'Tree canopy calculator', 'Waste and recycling strategy', 'Water environment assessment'.

issues.detail: The minerals and waste validation requirements appear only as guidance-link fragments in tab_items, never as requirements with triggers. Borehole or trial pit analysis: all mineral extraction. Geodiversity assessment: sites with designated or notable geological features. Details of storage, treatment or disposal of waste: new or extended landfill, hazardous waste, incineration. Restoration strategy and aftercare: any ground disturbance. Hydrological/hydrogeological assessment: where dewatering is proposed.
issues.evidence: Supporting information page, 'Mineral and waste:' headings 18-22.

issues.detail: Single source items are split into several rows. Agricultural dwelling appraisal and ALC/Soils share one fragment. Employment/Economic Statement and Marketing/vacancy evidence are both the Evidence of marketing statement. Drainage Strategy/SuDS and Foul Sewage/Utilities Statement are both the foul drainage text. Floor plans/Elevations and Schedule of works both quote the internal elevations text.
issues.evidence: Identical or overlapping trigger_excerpt values across these app_type_rows.

summary: Grokbot's link redirects to Buckinghamshire's current Local Validation List web page, which has been in force since 1 April 2020, not undated. The extraction is poor. Tab items are guidance fragments. Advisory 'additional documents' are treated as requirements. Householder and LBC rows are misassigned. Triggers mostly quote the rationale instead of the thresholds. About a dozen real requirements are missing, among them FRA, SuDS, waste and recycling, and new dwellings schedule.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
